newsitem.title: SWEDEN: Swedish shares end higher on international trends.
newsitem.headline: Swedish shares end higher on international trends.

text.p: Swedish shares ended higher on Friday, lifted by favorable international trends and lower interest rates.
The general index rose 0.59 percent to 2,327.63 in turnover totalling 5.35 billion crowns.
Banking group S-E-Banken was the most traded share by volume and rose one crown to 67 crowns on speculation that the bank would merge with banking group Nordbanken or insurer Skandia, dealers said.
"At the beginning of January something will surely turn up," a trader said.
Nordbanken plummeted eight crowns to 208.5 crowns on continued profit-taking after soaring during the first three days of the week. Skandia rose 4.5 crowns to 186.5 crowns.
Pharmaceutical company Astra rose 2.5 crowns to 328 crowns and rival Pharmacia & Upjohn followed suit, up 2.5 crowns to 264.5 crowns.
Dealers forecast that indices will keep rising, at least until the end of the year.
"As long as interest rates are falling, the rise does not seem to have a limit," a trader said.
